title: pyrus malus subsp. sylvestris
intro: Pyrus malus subsp. sylvestris, commonly known as Wild Apple, is a subspecies of the common apple tree found in the wild. It is a deciduous tree with edible fruits, leaves, and flowers that have been used in traditional medicine for their health benefits. The fruits of Pyrus malus subsp. sylvestris are rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals, offering potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which can aid in digestion, reduce fever, and support immune function. The bioactive constituents of Wild Apple include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which exhibit therapeutic actions like anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities.
